column1:
Aggressive
deepening of
our
dominance
in the
Kenya Market
column2:
• Economic activity declined
significantly in 2020
on account of covid-19
pandemic. Containment
measures put in place
significantly impacted
businesses and households.
Real (GDP) growth is
estimated at 0.6 % in 2020.
• Inflation was well anchored
in 2020
• Kenya shilling depreciated
by 4.4%
• Market capitalization
declined in 2020.
• Corporate income tax for
resident companies revised
from 30% to 25% for 2020.
• Central Bank of Kenya issued
emergency measures to
facilitate mobile money
transactions that resulted in
fee waivers. The regulator
also issued emergency
measures on restructuring of
loans for
• bank borrowers that resulted
in waiver of some credit
related fees.
• Strong credit growth was
witnessed in manufacturing,
transport & communication,
Agriculture, Real estate &
consumer durables.
• Favorable regulatory
environment
• Operationalization of credit
guarantee scheme – (de-risk
lending to MSMEs).
column3:
• Reduced earning
margins from a
tough operating
environment
and Fee waivers
issued by the
Regulator.
• Increased Gross
Non-Performing
Loans in
impacted
sectors such
as Transport,
Tourism and
Trade.
• Increased
competition
from Bank and
Non-Bank in the
sectors/segments
that are least
impacted by the
pandemic.
column4:
• Opportunity to
leverage business
models to grow in
sectors that are still
vibrant.
• Opportunity to
increase lending to
the MSMEs space
taking advantage
of the credit
guarantee scheme.
• Opportunity to
deepen the use
of alternative
delivery channels
to increase lending
and non-funded
income.
• Lower costs due
to efficiency
as consumers
prefer contactless
banking.
• Opportunity to
partner with long
term funding
partners and
the Government
in supporting
economic growth
through lending.
column5:
• Ensuring that we maintain strong capital
buffers to support growth. We continue
to operate in a profitable manner hence
increasing our retained earnings.
• Ongoing transformation initiatives which
are key enablers in market dominance.
We are constantly optimizing our business
models and reviewing our products to
ensure that we are growing our loan book,
deposit book and NFI despite the tough
operating environment.
• Lending to MSMEs through the Credit
Guarantee scheme is ongoing.
• 92% of our transactions are through
alternative channels responding to our
customer preference for contactless
banking.
• Proactive provisioning and facilities
restructures for credit risk management.
• Ongoing Credit Review Implementation
Project “Project Kilele” with McKinsey &Co.
that aims at improving the end to end
credit management in the Bank.
• Ongoing Project 3C (Connect, Collect,
Cure) that has decentralized NPL
collections.
• Optimal risk spread in the various
interest earning assets, optimizing our
Government Securities investment.
• Long term funding partners to support
sustainable financing to MSMEs,
Agriculture, climate smart initiatives and
the health sector.
• Ongoing partnerships with non-bank
financial institutions though open banking
to enhance growth in the various sectors.
